newsitem.title: JAPAN: FEATURE - Japan pet-lovers can rent by the hour.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE - Japan pet-lovers can rent by the hour.

text.p: A Tokyo pet shop owner is offering animal lovers in crowded Japan a rental-pet service as an alternative to buying a four-legged companion.
With more than 12.5 million people jammed into the capital, apartment managers often have strict rules prohibiting ownership of dogs or cats.
Rental contracts usually have a "no pets" clause, and flats that allow animals are so rare that property agents find it easier to list the few exceptions.
So, hundreds of would-be pet owners are making tracks to Masahiro Kobayashi and his "Perro Moco" rent-a-pet shop.
Kobayashi said he came up with the idea about eight years ago as a service to Japanese production houses making films or TV commercials.
Since the animals being used in films were not getting enough attention when off camera, Kobayashi decided to give ordinary people a chance to rent them as well.
"People in Japan often just don't have the space or permission to keep pets inside their homes, so it's a temporary solution for the children or elderly people who want animals around," he said.
Yasuo and Yukari Yamamoto have been patrons for several years and, like many regulars, they have formed a pet-owner relationship with some of the animals.
About once a week, the couple picks up Little, a golden retriever, and Chaco, a mini-dachshund, for walks at a nearby Tokyo park where they mingle with other pet lovers.
Despite the hassles of temporary pet ownership, such as cleaning up after their charges, the Yamamotos keep coming back for more.
"We live in a small apartment where we aren't allowed to keep pets, but I've always wanted to have one," said Yukari as she stroked Chaco's auburn coat.
Kobayashi says many pet renters have "favourites" among the 15 dogs and 15 cats, some for sale, that are kept at the shop.
Of his 30 to 50 customers per month, most are young couples on dates or potential pet owners who want a trial run, Kobayashi said.
A four-hour walk with a cat or a small dog costs about 3,000 yen (US $24.60). Larger dogs cost 5,000 yen ($41). Professional renters such as film studios pay 10 times as much.
